findings.issue: Before assigning an invocation id, capturing the code revision, or writing an operation record/handoff, __call__ returns WorkerWorkflowOutcome(status="blocked") when the launch/check/queue identity or queue state mismatches. This path produces no substantive per-stage handoffs and prevents downstream report/fallback work. run_worker_once later observes only the non-complete outcome and terminal reconciliation can mark the workflow incomplete; the reviewer found no provider handoff for the precondition failure itself. This is a future blocked workflow result and a continuation gap for an operation-level identity/state mismatch.
findings.evidence: Static source inspection at workflow_provider.py:501-517, with call flow continuing directly to invocation_id/capture only after the early return. FC09 test-results.json and final JUnit cover schema-15 migration and publication crash/resume, but not this precondition path. The explicit 2026-10-19 exclusion check is included in the helper and must remain intact.
findings.requested_fix: Keep the 2026-10-19 no-dispatch rule and never execute work with an untrusted/mismatched identity. For identity/queue-state mismatch, emit a correlated concrete unknown/not_performed operation and content-bearing safe handoffs (or a controller fallback handoff naming the supplied and expected safe identity fields) so the reporter/downstream owner is still started; do not return a future blocked stage/workflow result or silently omit the reason.
findings.impact: The workflow can terminate without invoking required later owners or recording why the stage chain did not start, contrary to the no-gate/content-bearing continuation contract.
